chapter: Western University and Kansas City nightlife
title: Countess Johnson and other women pianists
summary: Countess Johnson replaced Mary Lou Williams with Kirk, died young; another woman pianist played across the street.

bands.name: Andy Kirk and His Clouds of Joy

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well, now, Countess Johnson, who was she?
That's the lady that took Mary Lou Williams' place, in Andy Kirk's band; she didn't live long. She was a young girl.
What was the matter with her?
She died of tuberculosis, or so they thought, you know.
Very good. Everybody said she was better than Mary Lou.
There was another woman named Esther--what was that child's name?

There was another woman named Etta, or sump'n like that, played across the street from us who was the queen of all of 'em. She only played and sang alone. But she'd come into those jam sessions, and tear up some of those men. She and her husband just played it alone over in that little club and they made good money. (inaudible)
Well, it's very interesting, you know, I know that name Countess Johnson, but I've never heard anything about her. She was really a good pianist?
Yeah. And I'll have to go back again. We got away from Western University.
I know. But you were still were going in from Western?
Yeah. Allen, I'll give you a description, I'll give you a story that brings you in what's-er-name. Then I'll go back to Western University.
